title: Underfloor Radiant Heating Pipe Layout
prompt:
Create a single HTML file using Three.js (via CDN) that implements an interactive underfloor radiant heating pipe layout designer and thermal simulator.

## Scene Setup
- Create a 10x10 unit floor slab rendered as a flat plane with a subtle concrete texture (procedural gray with noise). The slab sits at Y=0.
- Use an OrbitControls camera starting at position (0, 12, 12) looking at the center of the floor.
- Add ambient light (intensity 0.4) and a directional light from (5, 10, 5) with intensity 0.8.
- Draw a thin grid overlay on the floor (1-unit spacing, 10x10 = 100 cells). Each cell is 1x1 unit.
- The floor is divided into two zones: Zone A (left 5 columns, x: 0-4) and Zone B (right 5 columns, x: 5-9).

## Pipe Layout System
- The user places radiant heating pipes on the grid. Pipes are rendered as colored TubeGeometry segments (radius 0.06) that follow grid edges (not diagonals).
- Pipe placement mode: user clicks on a grid cell center to start a pipe run, then clicks adjacent cells sequentially to extend the pipe. Each segment connects cell centers along grid lines (horizontal or vertical only, no diagonal).
- Pressing 'Enter' finalizes the current pipe run. Pressing 'Escape' cancels the current in-progress run.
- Each finalized pipe run is assigned to whichever zone the majority of its cells fall in.
- Zone A pipes are colored blue (0x3366ff), Zone B pipes are colored red (0xff3333).
- Maximum total pipe length across both zones is 80 segments. Display remaining capacity.

## Thermal Simulation
- Each grid cell has a temperature value. Initial temperature is 15°C for all cells.
- When the user clicks a 'Simulate' button, run a thermal diffusion simulation:
  - Cells containing pipe segments are heat sources at 40°C.
  - Each simulation step: for every non-pipe cell, new temp = old temp + 0.2 * (avg neighbor temp - old temp). Neighbors are the 4 adjacent cells (or fewer at edges).
  - Run 20 steps automatically with a 100ms interval between steps.
  - Visualize temperature on the floor by coloring each cell: interpolate from blue (15°C) through green (25°C) to red (40°C).
- After simulation completes, compute and display zone average temperatures.

## Flow Rate Controls
- Add a DOM slider for each zone (Zone A Flow Rate, Zone B Flow Rate) ranging from 0.0 to 1.0 (step 0.1, default 0.5).
- Flow rate acts as a multiplier on the heat source temperature: effective source temp = 15 + (40 - 15) * flowRate.
- Changing flow rate and re-running simulation uses the new effective source temperatures.

## HUD / UI
- Top-left HUD panel showing:
  - Current mode: 'Idle' | 'Placing' | 'Simulating' | 'Complete'
  - Total pipe segments placed
  - Remaining pipe capacity (80 - total)
  - Zone A segment count and Zone B segment count
  - Zone A avg temp and Zone B avg temp (after simulation)
  - Current simulation step (0-20)
- Buttons: 'Simulate' (runs simulation), 'Reset Temps' (resets all temps to 15°C and clears coloring), 'Clear All Pipes' (removes all pipes and resets everything).
- Zone flow rate sliders below the buttons.

## State Management
Expose window.__3D_STATE__ with:
- mode: string ('idle'|'placing'|'simulating'|'complete')
- totalSegments: number (total pipe segments placed)
- remainingCapacity: number (80 - totalSegments)
- zoneASegments: number
- zoneBSegments: number
- pipeRuns: number (count of finalized pipe runs)
- simulationStep: number (0 before sim, increments to 20)
- zoneAAvgTemp: number (average temperature of Zone A cells)
- zoneBAvgTemp: number (average temperature of Zone B cells)
- globalAvgTemp: number (average temperature of all 100 cells)
- maxTemp: number (highest cell temperature)
- minTemp: number (lowest cell temperature)
- zoneAFlowRate: number (current slider value)
- zoneBFlowRate: number (current slider value)
- gridTemps: 2D array [10][10] of current cell temperatures
- currentRunLength: number (segments in the current in-progress run, 0 if idle)
- heatSourceCount: number (number of unique cells that contain pipe segments)

Update __3D_STATE__ in real-time as state changes.
physics_constraints: Thermal diffusion must follow the discrete update rule: newTemp = oldTemp + 0.2 * (avgNeighborTemp - oldTemp). Heat source cells are clamped to their effective source temperature each step. All temperatures must remain in [15, 40] range. Zone averages must be arithmetic means of their respective 50 cells. Total segments must equal zoneASegments + zoneBSegments. Remaining capacity must equal 80 - totalSegments.
